post.title: Granite in clear water
post.body:
These are from the morning of September 12, a little after ten.

The first three were taken within two minutes of each other, looking down on a small cove. Pines come right down to a strip of pale sand. Granite boulders are scattered through the shallows, some sitting high and dry and bleached white on top, others just under the surface. The water is clear enough that you can follow the rocks out until the turquoise shallows drop off into deep blue.

In the third shot the sun is catching the water in the lower right corner and washing it out. I kept it anyway, because the boulders in the middle are the sharpest of the set.

The last photo is from about an hour later and looks straight down. From directly overhead the boulders turn into simple shapes: white tops, darker rims of submerged rock, and the green-brown of everything under the water. Two people are in the frame, small enough that they are just part of the pattern: one swimming at the upper right, one near a rock in the middle.

The straight-down view was the one worth waiting for. From an angle the cove looks like a postcard. From directly above it looks like a map.

episode.title: Straight down
episode.script:
September twelfth, just after ten in the morning, high above a small cove where the pines come all the way down to the water.

The first pictures came quickly, three of them in under two minutes. A strip of pale sand. Granite boulders scattered through the shallows, their tops bleached almost white. And water so clear you could follow the rocks out, one after another, until the turquoise gave way to deep blue.

In one of them the sun had caught the surface and washed out a corner of the frame. Christian kept it anyway. The boulders in the middle were the sharpest of the morning, and he could tell a flaw in the corner from a flaw in the picture. That's an eye, not luck.

***

Then came a long pause. About an hour of it.

When the last picture came, it looked straight down. From directly overhead, the cove stopped looking like a postcard and started looking like a map. White tops. Dark rims of rock just under the surface. The green and brown of everything below the water. Somewhere in all of it, two people so small they became part of the pattern, one of them swimming.

Four pictures, out of a whole morning. He knew which angle mattered, and he waited for it.

***

Some mornings tell you everything from the ground. This one needed a little height.
